outcome: Not settled as of 13 Oct 2026. Since 26 Jan 2024: a 2025 construction (Appleby, Flammia, Kopp) gives a valid SIC in every dimension d>3 only conditionally on two number-theoretic conjectures; a Sept 2026 preprint (Radchenko, Wheeler) proves a family of quadratic Stark-unit relations that Appleby, Flammia and Kopp conjectured (Wikipedia's SIC-POVM article says it settles a conjecture the AFK route relied on; the abstract does not say that); numerical SICs were added in 17 dimensions (2024, conjectural method) and in dimension 100 (2025); and a single-author claimed unconditional proof (Joka, Jan 2026) was withdrawn by its author in May 2026 with the comment that the proof is not correct.
problem_asks: Whether a SIC-POVM exists in every finite dimension d: d^2 unit vectors (rank-one elements) in complex C^d whose pairwise squared overlaps all equal 1/(d+1). Parts: (a) existence for each d (d=1 is trivial); (b) the universal claim over all d, not finitely many d; (c) no explicit construction or proof method is asked for. The statement itself does not require Weyl-Heisenberg covariance or a fiducial-eigenvector condition; those appear in Zauner's original formulation and in most known constructions, so events that settle only WH-covariant SICs are a scope point to be recorded, not a restatement of the bullet.

events.what_happened: Renes, Blume-Kohout, Scott and Caves, 'Symmetric Informationally Complete Quantum Measurements' (arXiv quant-ph/0310075; later journal publication not checked). Constructs SIC-POVMs explicitly in dimensions two, three and four, and conjectures group-covariant SICs for arbitrary d, with numerical support up to d=45.
events.delivers: Exact SIC-POVMs in d=2, 3 and 4 only. The general existence claim is conjectural; numerical support to d=45 is evidence, not a proof.
events.remains: Every d>=5 individually; the all-dimension claim.
events.directly_checkable: The d=2, 3, 4 SICs are small explicit matrices; I did not check them.
events.direction: Supports existence (explicit small cases and a conjecture for all d); does not settle the all-dimension question.
events.object: Explicit SIC-POVMs (sets of d^2 rank-one projectors with equal pairwise overlaps) in dimensions 2, 3 and 4, given by explicit construction.

events.what_happened: Hall and Rao, 'SIC-POVMs exist in all dimensions' (arXiv:0707.3002). The v1 claim (existence for all d>1) was seen only in a search summary of its abstract, not in the page itself; the page I opened shows only the withdrawal of v2.
events.delivers: Claimed existence in all dimensions d>1 (per the search summary of v1). Withdrawn; establishes nothing.
events.doubts: Withdrawn by the author for mathematical errors.

withdrawn.what: v2 withdrawn; comment reads: This paper has been withdrawn by the author due to mathematical errors.

events.direction: Claimed to cut for existence; withdrawn, so no weight.

events.what_happened: Scott and Grassl, 'SIC-POVMs: A new computer study' (arXiv:0910.5784). Numerical search for d^2 equiangular lines; reports numerical solutions in all dimensions d<=67, a putatively complete list of Weyl-Heisenberg covariant SICs for d<=50, and new algebraic solutions in d=24, 35 and 48 alongside algebraic ones for d=4-15 and 19.
events.revisions: v1 30 Oct 2009; v2 16 Dec 2009 (further algebraic solutions for d=11 and d=14).
events.delivers: Numerical SICs for every d<=67; exact ones for the listed dimensions. Nothing for d>=68 and no general claim.
events.remains: All d>=68; exact solutions for most d; the all-dimension claim.
events.directly_checkable: Numerical fiducial vectors are in the paper's tables; I did not check them.
events.direction: Supports existence (numerical in d<=67); not a general result.
events.object: Numerical SIC fiducial vectors for every d<=67 (numerical, not exact, in most dimensions) and exact fiducials for the listed dimensions.

events.what_happened: Grassl and Scott, 'Fibonacci-Lucas SIC-POVMs' (arXiv:1707.02944). Reports exact solutions in d=4, 8, 19, 48, 124 and 323, within a conjectured Fibonacci-Lucas family, and a numerical solution in d=844.
events.revisions: v1 10 Jul 2017; v2 21 Sep 2017 (adds the exact d=323 solution; d=844 numerics to 150 digits).
events.delivers: Exact solutions in the six listed dimensions; the family behind them is conjectural.
events.remains: All other dimensions; the family conjecture; the all-dimension claim.
events.directly_checkable: The exact d=323 fiducial is a finite algebraic object; I did not check it.
events.doubts: The family is a conjecture; the abstract calls the solutions support for it.
events.direction: Supports existence in six dimensions; the family conjecture is not settled by these.
events.object: Exact SIC fiducials in d=4, 8, 19, 48, 124 and 323 (algebraic, explicit), and a numerical fiducial in d=844.

events.what_happened: Fuchs, Hoang and Stacey, 'The SIC Question: History and State of Play' (arXiv:1703.07901), a survey. Abstract as read: computer calculations have furnished solutions in all dimensions up to 151 and in some cases up to 844; the new solutions exhibit an additional symmetry and verify a conjecture of Zauner in many new cases.
events.revisions: v1 23 Mar 2017; v2 8 Apr 2017; v3 11 Jul 2017 (current; updated bibliography and dimension limit).
events.delivers: Compiles numerical solutions for all d<=151; some larger d up to 844. Verifies symmetry conjectures in many cases. No general claim.
events.remains: d>151 for all cases; exact solutions; the all-dimension claim.
events.direction: Supports existence numerically up to d=151; no general claim.

events.what_happened: Kopp, 'SIC-POVMs and the Stark conjectures' (arXiv:1807.05877). Proves, conditionally on a suitable set of real units in a ray class field, that a SIC-POVM can be built when d is an odd prime congruent to 2 mod 3; numerical verification in d=5, 11, 17 and 23. A journal version (IMRN 2021) was reported in a search summary, not opened.
events.delivers: Conditional construction for odd primes d=2 mod 3 given the real-units input; numerical checks in d=5, 11, 17, 23. Nothing unconditional.
events.remains: All other dimensions; the real-units input; the all-dimension claim.
events.doubts: Conditional on a Stark-type input, which is the same circle of ideas the 2025 AFK paper relies on.
events.direction: Supports existence conditionally in a restricted family of dimensions.

events.what_happened: Appleby, Bengtsson, Grassl, Harrison and McConnell, 'SIC-POVMs from Stark units: Prime dimensions n^2+3' (arXiv:2112.05552). Gives a recipe, conjectured to work, that uses a Stark unit from a ray class field of a real quadratic field to seed a SIC; reports such structures in thirteen prime dimensions of the form n^2+3, the largest p=19603. The abstract does not claim a general proof.
events.delivers: Existence in thirteen prime dimensions n^2+3 (as stated), by a recipe whose correctness rests on Stark conjectures. Not a general result.
events.remains: Every other dimension, including non-prime n^2+3 and the rest of the integers; the all-dimension claim.
events.doubts: Stated in the abstract as dependent on Stark conjectures.
events.direction: Supports existence in a restricted family of dimensions, conditionally.

events.what_happened: Samuel and Gedik, 'Group Theoretical Classification of SIC-POVMs' (arXiv:2401.11026, v1 posted 19 Jan 2024, before the frozen revision). Numerical classification of SIC Gram matrices in dimensions 4-7 (about 1.7x10^6, 1.1x10^5, 169 and 50 matrices); in dimensions 4-6 one equivalence class, in dimension 7 two families. The abstract argues that group covariance may be necessary in dimensions 4 and 5. A journal publication (J. Phys. A 57(29), 2024) was reported in a search result citing the Sabanci repository; I did not open the journal page.
events.delivers: Classification of numerical SIC Gram matrices restricted to dimensions 4-7. Adds no existence in any new dimension.
events.remains: Everything in the statement; existence in all dimensions.
events.doubts: Numerical, restricted to dimensions 4-7; the classification claim is the authors' own.
events.direction: Neither cuts for nor against existence.

events.what_happened: Bengtsson, Grassl and McConnell, 'SIC-POVMs from Stark Units: Dimensions n^2+3=4p, p prime' (arXiv:2403.02872, posted 5 Mar 2024). Extends the 2021 Stark-unit recipe to dimensions n^2+3=4p; gives solutions in seventeen such dimensions, reaching d=39604, with several improvements over the earlier paper. The introduction says: We have not been able to prove that the algorithm that we propose works in all dimensions. Published as J. Math. Phys. 66, 082202 (2025) (journal reference on the arXiv abstract page).
events.revisions: v1 only, 5 Mar 2024; journal version J. Math. Phys. 66, 082202 (2025).
events.delivers: SIC solutions in seventeen dimensions of the form n^2+3=4p (up to d=39604), produced by a conjectural algorithm seeded by Stark units; the authors do not prove the algorithm works in any untested dimension. Restricted to those seventeen dimensions; no general existence result.
events.remains: Every dimension outside the seventeen listed; the all-dimension claim; whether the seventeen dimensions are new to the numerical record was not checked against the pre-2024 table.

checked_by.who: Journal of Mathematical Physics (peer-reviewed journal; referees not named)
checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper as J. Math. Phys. 66, 082202 (2025), per the arXiv journal-reference field; the journal page itself was not opened

events.directly_checkable: The fiducial vectors in the listed dimensions can be checked numerically (overlaps equal to 1/(d+1)); I did not check them.
events.doubts: The method is conjectural by the authors' own statement; the Stark-unit inputs are conjectural; the abstract as read does not say whether the vectors are exact or numerical.
events.direction: Cuts for existence in the listed dimensions; does not establish existence elsewhere.
events.object: SICs (d^2 equal-overlap vectors) in seventeen dimensions d=n^2+3=4p with p prime, up to d=39604, each built from a single Stark unit in a ray class field of a real quadratic field used as seed. Constructed by an algorithm, not a non-constructive existence proof; whether the output is exact or numerical is not stated in the text I read.

events.what_happened: Kopp and Lagarias, 'SIC-POVMs and orders of real quadratic fields' (arXiv:2407.08048). Checks for 4 <= d <= 90 that the number of known geometric classes of Weyl-Heisenberg SICs equals the size of the ideal class monoid of the real quadratic order of discriminant (d+1)(d-3). Conjectures this for all d>=4 (Geometric Count Conjecture); proves that the conjecture implies more than one WH SIC class for every d>22; refines the Appleby-Flammia-McConnell-Yard class-field hypothesis (conjectural).
events.revisions: v1 10 Jul 2024; v2 27 Sep 2024; v3 28 Dec 2024; v4 14 May 2026 (current; 40 pages, 4 tables, 2 figures).
events.delivers: Structural conjectures about the number of WH-covariant SIC classes, checked for d<=90; a conditional statement that more than one class exists for d>22 if the conjecture holds. Establishes no existence in any new dimension.
events.remains: Existence in every dimension; the Geometric Count Conjecture for d>90 and in general.
events.doubts: The count identity is conjectural beyond d=90; the multiple-class result is conditional on it.
events.direction: Neither cuts for nor against existence; a structural conjecture about how many classes exist.

events.what_happened: Samuel and Gedik, 'SIC-POVMs and the Knaster's Conjecture' (arXiv:2405.16733, posted 27 May 2024). Uses a Bloch-sphere geometric view to prove Knaster's conjecture for the n vertices of an n-simplex (journal abstract), and deduces a continuous family of generalized SIC-POVMs in which n^2-1 elements share the same Tr(rho^3). The abstract states that the general proof of SIC existence is still an open problem. Published in J. Math. Phys. 66(9), 2025, DOI 10.1063/5.0222241.
events.revisions: v1 only, 27 May 2024; journal version J. Math. Phys. 66(9), 2025.
events.delivers: A geometric result on the Knaster problem and a continuous family of generalized SIC-POVMs (not the standard rank-one SICs as the problem uses the term). Does not establish any standard SIC in any dimension; the authors state general existence remains open.
events.remains: Existence of standard SICs in every dimension; the all-dimension claim.

checked_by.who: Journal of Mathematical Physics (peer-reviewed journal; referees not named)
checked_by.what_they_did: published the paper as J. Math. Phys. 66(9), 2025, DOI 10.1063/5.0222241, per the Sabanci repository record

events.doubts: The arXiv and journal abstracts differ in wording about the scope of the Knaster result (noted in a search summary; I did not compare the published text).
events.direction: Neither cuts for nor against standard SIC existence; the authors say the general question is open.
events.object: A continuous family of generalized SIC-POVMs in which n^2-1 of the elements share the same Tr(rho^3) value; explicit geometric construction; 10^4 generalized SIC-POVMs generated numerically in dimension 3.

events.what_happened: Kopp, 'The Shintani-Faddeev modular cocycle: Stark units from q-Pochhammer ratios' (arXiv:2411.06763). Abstract as read: gives a new interpretation of Stark units for real quadratic fields as real multiplication values of a modular cocycle, and proves a refinement of Shintani's Kronecker limit formula relating square roots of Stark class invariants to cocycle values.
events.revisions: v1 11 Nov 2024; v2 10 Dec 2024; v3 3 May 2025 (current).
events.delivers: A refinement of Shintani's Kronecker limit formula on Stark units for real quadratic fields. The abstract does not say it proves the special value identity used in the AFK construction, and it does not mention SICs or Zauner's conjecture.
events.remains: Everything in the Zauner statement; whether this result touches the AFK special value identity is not established by the abstract.
events.direction: Neither cuts for nor against existence directly; a number-theory input on the Stark side of the AFK route.

events.what_happened: Iverson and Mixon, 'Asymmetric SICs over finite fields' (arXiv:2506.20778). Constructs infinitely many new SICs over finite fields, some with trivial automorphism group; conjectures totally asymmetric SICs exist in infinitely many dimensions over finite fields. Zauner's conjecture is quoted only as background.
events.delivers: SICs over finite fields, an analogue setting. Says nothing about complex SICs in C^d.
events.direction: Neither cuts for nor against complex SIC existence; a different field.

events.what_happened: Fallon, 'Equiangular tight frames in real symplectic space: Zauner's conjecture and the skew Hadamard conjecture' (arXiv:2509.14463). Defines a symplectic analogue of equiangular tight frames over real symplectic space and states that the symplectic Zauner conjecture is equivalent to the skew Hadamard conjecture.
events.delivers: An equivalence between a real symplectic analogue and the skew Hadamard conjecture. Says nothing about complex SIC-POVMs in C^d.
events.direction: Neither cuts for nor against complex SIC existence; a different setting.

events.what_happened: Bengtsson and Grassl, 'A Conjecture on Almost Flat SIC-POVMs' (arXiv:2512.13201). Investigates a conjectured identity for SICs with anti-unitary symmetry, which expresses Stark units as sums of products; the abstract asks whether the identity determines these Stark units and answers: The answer is no, but the failure might be quite mild. The introduction says the obstruction may be quite mild.
events.delivers: A negative answer to whether the identity alone determines the Stark units. Constructs no SIC in any dimension and proves no existence result.
events.doubts: Whether the identity studied here is the same as the AFK special value identity is not stated in the text I read.
events.direction: Neither cuts for nor against existence; bears on the Stark-unit route.

events.what_happened: Appleby, Flammia and Kopp, 'A Constructive Approach to Zauner's Conjecture via the Stark Conjectures' (arXiv:2501.03970). Proposes a construction of d^2 complex equiangular lines in C^d using a ghost SIC built from real multiplication values of the Shintani-Faddeev modular cocycle, Galois conjugate to a true SIC; the authors call the resulting list putatively complete for Weyl-Heisenberg SICs in all d>3. The abstract says they prove the construction gives a valid SIC in every case assuming two conjectures. Also reports four numerical d=100 examples (three new) and conditional r-SIC generalisations. Talks by Flammia at QuICS (12 Mar 2025) and CodEx. No journal publication found.
events.revisions: v1 7 Jan 2025 (no comment); v2 17 Mar 2025, fix typos and some errors in the data tables, streamlined appendix D; 177 pages (130 main, 47 appendices), 6 figures.
events.delivers: Conditional on (i) the order-1 abelian Stark conjecture for real quadratic fields and (ii) a special value identity for the Shintani-Faddeev modular cocycle (the introduction, as read, names Theorem 1.4 as: The Stark Conjecture and the Twisted Convolution Conjecture together imply Zauner's conjecture), a valid WH-covariant SIC in every dimension d>3, described as putatively complete. Unconditionally: four numerical d=100 examples; d=100 already had numerical solutions from the 2009 and 2017 work, so this does not change which dimensions are covered.
events.remains: Unconditional existence in every dimension; both conjectures; the completeness claim (stated only as putative); SICs that are not Weyl-Heisenberg covariant.
events.time_since_posted: about 9 months (to 13 Oct 2026); no journal publication found
events.directly_checkable: The d=100 numerical fiducials and the conditional construction's overlap identities could be checked numerically; I did not check them.
events.doubts: Conditional on two conjectures, neither proved in any source I found. The conjecture is named differently in the abstract (special value identity) and in the introduction (Twisted Convolution Conjecture), and I could not confirm they are the same input. The completeness claim is stated only as putative. No referee report or journal version found. The 2026 Radchenko-Wheeler paper engages with a family of relations this paper conjectured (see later_work_cites_it); that is engagement, not verification.
events.direction: Cuts toward existence in every dimension d>3, conditionally on two number-theoretic conjectures; does not prove it.
events.object: A ghost SIC: a Weyl-Heisenberg-covariant fiducial built from real multiplication values of the Shintani-Faddeev modular cocycle, shown (under the Stark conjecture) to be Galois conjugate to an actual SIC and (under the special value identity) to give an idempotent presumptive fiducial projector. Explicit numerical examples: four nonequivalent SICs in d=100, three of them new, cross-validated against the Scott-Grassl numerics.

events.what_happened: Joka, 'Symmetric Informationally Complete Positive Operator Valued Measure and Zauner conjecture' (arXiv:2601.13475). Claims that in a Hilbert space of any finite dimension N there are N^2 unit vectors forming a SIC-POVM. Posted 20 Jan 2026 and revised four times; withdrawn by the author on 31 May 2026 with the comment The proof the paper gives is not correct. The method, per search snippets I could not confirm from the paper body, uses symplectic toric geometry (Delzant's theorem) and a regular simplex inscribed in complex projective space; the arXiv page lists no affiliation, and a search snippet gave University of Belgrade.
events.revisions: v1 20 Jan 2026; v2 22 Jan 2026 (title per a search snippet: SIC - POVM and Zauner's conjecture, not verified on the page); v3 7 Feb 2026; v4 7 Mar 2026; v5 31 May 2026, withdrawn.
events.delivers: Claimed (in the abstract) existence of SIC-POVMs in every finite dimension. Withdrawn by the author; by the author's own comment the proof is not correct. Establishes nothing as a result.
events.remains: Everything in the statement, on the withdrawal.
events.time_since_posted: withdrawn after about four months (v5 on 31 May 2026); about 9 months old at the research date
events.doubts: The author's own withdrawal comment, The proof the paper gives is not correct. The argument's body was not readable to me (PDF returned binary; HTML version 404), so the method description rests on search snippets. No expert commentary, blog post or news found in my searches.

withdrawn.what: v5 withdrawn by the author; comment: The proof the paper gives is not correct.

events.direction: Claimed to cut for existence in all dimensions; withdrawn by the author, so no weight.

events.what_happened: Glazyrin, 'New constructions of optimal arrangements of 2d lines in C^d' (arXiv:2608.16116). A neighbouring problem, not Zauner's: constructs equiangular tight frames of size 2d in C^d (not d^2 lines) by tensor and doubling constructions from amicable pairs of real Hadamard matrices. Its AI-use section credits ChatGPT 4.6 Sol with literature search, light copyediting and with finding certain constructions.
events.delivers: New ETFs of size 2d in C^d, in families given by amicable Hadamard pairs (for example of order q+1 for prime powers q=3 mod 4). Not a SIC result: the statement asks about d^2 vectors, and this paper does not address them.
events.direction: Neither cuts for nor against SIC existence; a neighbouring problem.

systems.name: ChatGPT 4.6 Sol
systems.what_it_did: Per the paper's AI-use section: used for literature search and light copyediting throughout the paper; the constructions in Subsections 3.3 and 3.4 and the argument for Proposition 3 were found with AI assistance. The author states all text was written by the author. This is a neighbouring problem's result, not an AI contribution to SIC existence.
systems.basis_quote: The constructions in Subsections 3.3, 3.4 and the argument for Proposition 3 were found with AI assistance.

events.what_happened: Radchenko and Wheeler, 'Real quadratic fields and finite quantum dilogarithms I' (arXiv:2609.21892). Abstract: proves that Stark-Shintani ray class invariants (Stark units) attached to real quadratic fields are algebraic numbers; that they are special values of Faddeev's modular quantum dilogarithm and satisfy an overdetermined polynomial system; and proves a family of quadratic relations for Stark units recently conjectured by Appleby, Flammia and Kopp, motivated by Zauner's conjecture. Does not claim to settle Zauner's conjecture. Title suggests a first part.
events.revisions: v1 18 Sep 2026; v2 29 Sep 2026 (current; 36 pages, 1 figure per comments).
events.delivers: Algebraicity of Stark units for real quadratic fields (Theorem 1 as stated in the text I read, unconditional per the authors), and the quadratic relations AFK conjectured (as the abstract describes them). Does not claim the order-1 abelian Stark conjecture or the special value identity in full. Which AFK input this discharges is not stated in the text I read.
events.remains: Zauner's conjecture; whichever AFK input is not covered by the quadratic relations; the unconditional all-dimension existence.
events.directly_checkable: The overdetermined polynomial system for the special values (Equations 4-7 as read) could be checked by computer algebra; the paper reports computer algebra was used for a non-existence remark (Remark 6). I did not check it.
events.doubts: Preprint three to four weeks old with no review found. The title marks it as part I. Wikipedia's SIC-POVM article, as summarised to me by WebFetch, says the number-theoretic conjecture behind the AFK route was claimed to be settled by Radchenko and Wheeler in 2026; the abstract does not say so, and I found no other source confirming a settlement. Author names are from the arXiv abstract page; acknowledgement initials C.W. and D.R. are consistent with them.
events.direction: Cuts toward discharging part of the conditional input of the AFK route, per Wikipedia; the paper itself claims an algebraicity result and a family of relations, not a resolution of Zauner's conjecture.

disputes.summary: Wikipedia's SIC-POVM article (read through a WebFetch summary) says the AFK route relied on a number-theoretic conjecture that was claimed to be settled by Radchenko and Wheeler in 2026. The Radchenko-Wheeler abstract says they prove a family of quadratic relations for Stark units that AFK conjectured, and does not say they settle the conjecture AFK relied on. Which AFK input, if any, is discharged is not established from the text I could read.

AFK's abstract names the second assumption as a special value identity for the Shintani-Faddeev modular cocycle; its introduction (as read) states Theorem 1.4 as the Stark Conjecture and the Twisted Convolution Conjecture together imply Zauner's conjecture. Whether these name the same input is not established.

summary: Searches (42 web queries and about 60 page opens) found no unconditional resolution of Zauner's conjecture as of 13 Oct 2026, and no AI system credited with mathematics bearing on SIC existence. In-window events, in date order: Kopp-Lagarias (July 2024) and Bengtsson-Grassl-McConnell (5 Mar 2024, J. Math. Phys. 2025) add conjectural structure and solutions in seventeen dimensions n^2+3=4p up to d=39604; the authors state they cannot prove the algorithm works beyond the tested dimensions. Samuel-Gedik (27 May 2024) prove Knaster's conjecture for n-simplex vertices and a continuous family of generalized SIC-POVMs, and state general existence is open; their 19 Jan 2024 preprint predates the frozen revision and classifies numerical Gram matrices in dimensions 4-7. Appleby-Flammia-Kopp (7 Jan 2025) give a construction of SICs in every d>3 that is valid conditionally on two number-theoretic conjectures; their abstract reports four numerical d=100 examples, three new, though d=100 was already covered numerically by the 2009 and 2017 work; no journal version was found. Joka (20 Jan 2026) claimed an unconditional proof for all N; the author withdrew it on 31 May 2026 with the comment that the proof is not correct, and no expert engagement was found. Radchenko-Wheeler (18 Sep 2026) prove algebraicity of Stark units for real quadratic fields and a family of quadratic relations that AFK conjectured; their AI disclosure says LLMs were used only to check calculations and found mistakes in an earlier draft, with all final calculations verified by the authors. Analogues and neighbours that do not bear on complex SICs: Iverson-Mixon (finite fields, June 2025), Fallon (real symplectic, Sept 2025), Kopp (Stark units, Nov 2024), Bengtsson-Grassl (Dec 2025, identity does not determine Stark units), and Glazyrin (2d lines in C^d, Aug 2026), whose AI-use section credits ChatGPT 4.6 Sol with constructions; that is a different problem. Pre-window events give exact SICs in d<=4 (2003), numerical SICs for d<=67 (2009) and d<=151 (2017), exact d=323 (2017), a conditional family of primes (2018), n^2+3 prime dimensions (2021), and a 2007 claim withdrawn within three days. Close calls: (a) whether Radchenko-Wheeler discharge an AFK input: Wikipedia says yes; the abstract says they prove a conjectured family, which is narrower; (b) whether numerical SICs in listed dimensions move the problem: they give existence numerically in those dimensions, not rigorously; (c) whether the 2024 seventeen-dimension result is new to the numerical record: I did not compare against the pre-2024 tables; (d) whether Joka's withdrawal ends the matter: the withdrawal is the only author-side evidence, and no expert read the paper. A search for a Wikipedia article specifically on Zauner's conjecture did not surface one; I read the SIC-POVM article instead. A search for Terence Tao's blog found nothing on this topic.
competing_reading: Read the Wikipedia wording at face value and Radchenko-Wheeler discharges one of AFK's two conjectures, leaving the construction nearly unconditional and the Stark-side input as the only gap; the AFK paper would then be the strongest recent progress. The reverse reading: the Radchenko-Wheeler abstract proves algebraicity and a family of relations AFK conjectured, so both AFK inputs may remain open and the AFK theorem stays conditional. A second competing reading: count the 2024-2025 numerical solutions (BGM 2024, AFK 2025 d=100) as moving existence, since they add dimensions to a known-existence list; the opposing reading treats only proved or exact constructions as movement, and numerical solutions as evidence.
what_would_settle_it: (1) The full text of arXiv 2609.21892 (not readable through WebFetch) mapping its quadratic relations onto AFK's special value identity and Stark conjecture, and stating which, if any, is fully covered. (2) An expert review of AFK's conditional theorem, or a journal version. (3) An unconditional construction covering every dimension. (4) The v1 text of Joka's arXiv 2601.13475 and any comments before withdrawal, to confirm the claimed step. (5) The pre-2024 numerical tables compared with the BGM 2024 seventeen dimensions and the AFK d=100 examples, to settle novelty.
